overview: Both are abnormal chromosome numbers, but aneuploidy changes individual chromosomes while polyploidy multiplies whole chromosome sets.
genZNote: Aneuploidy: one chromosome shows up uninvited or ghosts the party. Polyploidy: the whole squad multiplied.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: Gain or loss of one or a few individual chromosomes from the normal diploid number.
aspects.valueB: Gain of one or more complete extra sets of chromosomes (3n, 4n, etc.).

aspects.label: Cause
aspects.valueA: Nondisjunction — failure of chromosomes to separate properly during meiosis or mitosis.
aspects.valueB: Failure of cytokinesis after chromosome duplication, or fusion of unreduced gametes.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueB: Triploid (3n) watermelons, many polyploid crop plants like wheat.

aspects.label: Common In
aspects.valueA: Well documented and often serious in animals/humans.
aspects.valueB: Very common and often beneficial in plants; rare and usually lethal in animals.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) is the classic human aneuploidy example tested repeatedly in NEET.
overlay.memoryTrick: Aneuploidy = a few chromosomes off. Polyploidy = whole extra sets.
overlay.commonMisconception: Polyploidy is not automatically harmful — in plants it's often associated with larger size and hybrid vigour.
